summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for management of a persistent migraine and worsening neuropathic pain following a lumbar puncture three months prior. She reported severe, constant headache with photophobia, phonophobia, and nausea, along with allodynia and stabbing neuropathic pain in her extremities. MRI and MRV of the brain showed no acute abnormalities or venous sinus thrombosis. Medication adjustments included discontinuation of Topamax, reduction of clonazepam, dextroamphetamine, and lamotrigine, and initiation of a cross-taper from fluoxetine to venlafaxine for potential dual benefit on mood and neuropathic pain. A small, resolving pneumoperitoneum was noted on abdominal imaging, likely unrelated to acute pathology and possibly associated with her peritoneal dialysis catheter. Peritoneal fluid cultures showed no growth, and labs for neuropathy workup were unremarkable. Insulin dosing was adjusted due to nocturnal hypoglycemia. She was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up planned in pain management and psychiatry.
